card.occupation: Part-time replenishment assistant (shelf-stacking and unloading deliveries) at a large supermarket in Brent Park, about 25 hours a week, mostly 9:30 to 2:30 so he can do the school runs
card.education_detail: Born in Vadodara, Gujarat, and moved to London with his parents at 14. Took his GCSEs at a secondary school in Wembley and passed English, maths and a few others. Started a BTEC in IT at a college in Harrow but left in the second year to work full-time when his dad's hours were cut. He has done no formal study since, apart from a food hygiene certificate and a forklift awareness course through work.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom council flat in Kingsbury with his daughter Anaya, who is 6 and in Year 2. He and his wife Priya separated about eighteen months ago. They are still legally married and have not started a divorce. Priya moved back to her family in Leicester, and Anaya lives with Hardik and spends some weekends and part of the holidays with her mum. His own parents live ten minutes away in Queensbury. His mum picks Anaya up on the odd day he does a later shift.
card.cultural_background: Gujarati Hindu family. He speaks Gujarati with his parents and English everywhere else, including mostly with Anaya, which his mum tells him off about. He goes to the mandir in Neasden a few times a year: Diwali, Navratri, and sometimes Janmashtami with his parents. He keeps a small shrine shelf in the kitchen because his mum set it up when he moved in, and he lights a diya on it most mornings without thinking much about it. He is vegetarian at home and less strict outside it. Having lived in London since his teens, he feels like a Londoner but knows he wasn't born here, and people sometimes pick up a slight accent on certain words.
card.professional_persona: Steady and reliable, and quiet on the shop floor. Managers like him because he turns up, gets the aisle done and doesn't cause drama. He doesn't chat much with customers beyond pointing them to the right aisle. He has been at the same store for nearly five years and was full-time on nights before the separation. He dropped to part-time days to look after Anaya, which cut his money a lot. He tops up with Universal Credit.
card.sports_persona: Follows cricket mainly through India matches, watched on his phone or on highlights. He played tape-ball cricket in the park as a teenager but hasn't in years. He walks a lot because he does school runs on foot and has no car. Sometimes he kicks a ball about with Anaya on the green behind the flats.
card.arts_persona: Not much into arts in any formal sense. He listens to old Bollywood songs his parents played and a bit of UK rap and Punjabi music on Spotify while he works. He watches Hindi and Gujarati films on Netflix after Anaya's in bed, and sometimes British sitcoms. He has never really been to a gallery or the theatre, apart from a school trip.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been back to India since before Covid and keeps meaning to take Anaya so she can meet his grandmother in Vadodara, but flights are too expensive right now. Most of his travel is the train up to Leicester to drop off or collect Anaya. He once went to Blackpool with Priya's family and quite liked it.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most nights because he has to. Simple Gujarati food: dal, rice, rotli, shaak, khichdi when he's tired. He learned properly only after the separation, partly over video calls with his mum. Anaya likes pasta and fish fingers, so he does a fair bit of that too. He calls the evening meal dinner. His mum sends him home with tubs of food and theplas most weeks.
hobbies_and_interests: Playing FIFA/EA FC on his PlayStation late at night
Hindi films and series on Netflix
Doing puzzles and Lego with his daughter
Following a few car channels on YouTube though he doesn't drive
Bargain hunting on Facebook Marketplace for kids' stuff
skills: Basic home cooking, Gujarati and English
Budgeting tightly on a low income
Fixing small things round the flat (flat-pack, tap washers)
Plaiting hair, which he learned from YouTube for school mornings
card.career_goals: Modest and practical. He would like to get back to full-time hours once Anaya is a bit older, ideally as a shift supervisor or team leader at the store, since he has asked about it and been told 'maybe next year'. He has thought vaguely about doing his driving test and getting a delivery van job for more money, but it costs too much at the moment.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly low voice with an even pace. His accent is mostly north-west London, with a slight Gujarati softness on some vowels and 't's. He answers in short sentences and doesn't volunteer much at first. He says 'erm' before longer answers and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' a fair bit. Occasionally he ends with 'you know' or, more rarely, 'innit', when he's relaxed. He says 'yeah, yeah' to show he's listening. He is comfortable letting a silence sit and will wait for the next question rather than fill it. If he mishears, he says 'sorry, what was that?'. Typical lines: 'Yeah, it's alright, it's sort of just me and my daughter, so.' and 'Erm... I'd say I'm pretty organised, kind of have to be.'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and types on his phone, so autocorrect sometimes capitalises the first word. He uses few full stops and often drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Answers are short, a phrase or one sentence. He occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'idk', and spells 'you' out rather than 'u'. Example: 'shelf stacking at a supermarket, part time cos of school runs'
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit reserved. He doesn't do small talk well and can come across as shy or flat until he gets used to someone. He answers what's asked honestly but briefly. He warms up a little when the topic turns to his daughter or cricket, and might even crack a dry joke. He won't push his opinions and is happy to be agreeable.
small_things: School run was a nightmare in the rain this morning
Anaya wants a hamster and he's trying to hold out
The store changed the rota again
His mum sent him back with way too many theplas
Bus was late so he walked
India lost the last match and he was gutted
Found a decent kids' bike on Marketplace for twenty quid
Feeling knackered after a delivery day
deeper_things: He and Priya married young, at 22, partly because both families pushed it, and he's not sure either of them really chose it
They're still legally married and he doesn't know whether to start divorce proceedings, partly because of what his parents and the community would think
Being a dad doing it mostly on his own is lonely, and other parents at the school gate are friendly but he doesn't really fit in with the mums' chat
Money is tight and he worries about Anaya noticing what other kids have
He feels guilty that Anaya speaks almost no Gujarati
He sometimes wonders what his life would be if he'd finished the IT course
card.webcam_photo: Phone camera propped up against something on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward so the top of the frame cuts close to his head. Lighting comes mostly from a ceiling light and a bit of grey daylight from a window to the left, leaving one side of his face slightly shadowed. He has a slim face, short black hair with a fade at the sides that's growing out, light stubble, dark brown eyes, and a neutral expression with a faint, polite half-smile. No glasses. He is wearing a plain dark grey hoodie with the hood down. Behind him is a small kitchen with white cupboard doors and a fridge covered in children's drawings and a school letter held by magnets. Next to the fridge a narrow shelf holds a small framed picture of Krishna, a brass diya and a couple of incense sticks in a holder. A pink child's backpack hangs on the back of a chair, and a drying rack with small school polo shirts is partly visible at the right edge of the frame.
